sermon.title: Act Like Men
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Samuel 4:9 that God’s people must act like champions—strong and ready to fight—and asks why Israel lost to the Philistines despite Hannah’s Spirit-led prayer. He compares Eli’s corrupt sons, everyone doing right in his own eyes, and prosperity and positive-thinking teaching with America’s decline since the great awakening. When Israel returned to God with all their hearts, the Lord thundered on their enemies.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check (as spoken, unverified): Southern Baptists, Methodists and Presbyterians founded on pro-slavery doctrine; the Pope declaring slavery okay for southern Catholics; church attendance 60% then 27% now; “fourth great awakening in 1948”; 1 Samuel 4:9 is spoken by the Philistines. Sensitive content kept as spoken: prosperity preachers named (Oral Roberts, Reverend Ike, A. A. Allen, T. L. Osborn, T. D. Jakes, Kenneth Copeland, Dollar, Tilton, Hagin, Osteen, Joyce Meyer); Norman Vincent Peale as Trump’s minister; Robert Schuller; Bill Gothard; Trump and Hillary; football players and the national anthem; homosexuality and same-sex marriage in churches; a congregant who died of cancer (unnamed).

faqs.question: Who said “quit you like men” in 1 Samuel 4:9?
faqs.answer: It was said to the Philistine army.

faqs.question: Is prayer alone enough?
faqs.answer: Prayer is part of the fight, but we must also speak and fight.

faqs.question: Does God make some poor?
faqs.answer: Hannah prayed that the Lord makes poor and makes rich.

faqs.question: Must you deny sickness to be healed?
faqs.answer: He tells of a woman harmed by refusing to admit she had cancer.

faqs.question: What does he say about seeker-friendly churches?
faqs.answer: They please men instead of God, like Eli’s sons.

faqs.question: Is God’s presence proof of approval?
faqs.answer: No—his presence is not his approval.

faqs.question: What is wrong with faith in your faith?
faqs.answer: Faith must be in Bible truths acted out.

faqs.question: When do we receive God’s promise?
faqs.answer: After we have done the will of God.

faqs.question: Does joining a church save you?
faqs.answer: No—you are saved by meeting Jesus Christ.
